An obstacle that prevents progress or agreement during a process or negotiation.
Disagreement over salary structure remained the main stumbling block in reaching a final employment contract.
turning point
A time at which a decisive change in a situation occurs, especially one with good results.
Winning the prestigious young national award marked a major turning point in her artistic career.
wake-up call
An event that acts as a warning, making people aware of a dangerous or bad situation.
The severe winter storm served as a wake-up call for the council to improve emergency flood defenses.
breathtaking view
An extremely beautiful, impressive or dramatic scene that fills a viewer with wonder.
Hikers reached the mountain summit and enjoyed a breathtaking view of the green valley below.
broad spectrum
A wide range of subjects, ideas, opinions, options or related scientific phenomena.
The research project covered a broad spectrum of environmental topics ranging from forestry to ocean conservation.
calculated risk
A chance taken after careful estimation of the possible outcomes, dangers and benefits.
Expanding into international markets was a calculated risk that ultimately doubled company sales within two years.
cautious optimism
A feeling of general hopefulness tempered by awareness of potential difficulties or risks.
Economic analysts expressed cautious optimism about market recovery following positive employment reports released this morning.
clear distinction
A sharp, noticeable and obvious difference between two similar things, ideas, concepts or categories.
There is a clear distinction between short term temporary relief measures and long term sustainable solutions.
cultural heritage
The legacy of physical artifacts and intangible attributes of a group inherited from past generations.
Preserving traditional folk music and craft techniques protects the cultural heritage of the island population.
dire consequences
Extremely serious, dangerous or terrible results that occur following a specific action or event.
Ignoring safety regulations when operating heavy factory machinery can lead to dire consequences for workers.
driving force
A power or influence that provides motive, momentum or guidance to a project or movement.
Her passion for social equality was the primary driving force behind her career in public policy.
foster growth
To encourage the development or growth of something positive, such as an economy or idea.
Government tax incentives were designed to foster growth in renewable energy industries across the country.
frequent flyer
A passenger who travels regularly on commercial aircraft, often earning loyalty rewards.
As a frequent flyer, he accumulated enough loyalty points to upgrade to business class on international flights.
long-term goal
A target or objective that requires planning and sustained effort over an extended period.
Her main long-term goal is to establish her own independent architectural design firm within ten years.
major breakthrough
An important discovery or progress that helps solve a notable problem or advance knowledge.
Developing an effective vaccine represented a major breakthrough in combating the infectious tropical virus worldwide.
necessary evil
Something that is undesirable or unpleasant but must be accepted to achieve a essential result.
Paying taxes is often viewed as a necessary evil to fund essential public services like healthcare.
peace of mind
A state of mental tranquility, security and freedom from worry, anxiety or fear.
Taking out comprehensive travel insurance gives holidaymakers complete peace of mind while exploring foreign countries.
root cause
The fundamental or primary reason why a specific problem or issue occurs.
Investigating the root cause of the engine failure prevented similar mechanical issues from happening again.
rough draft
A preliminary or unrefined version of a piece of writing, document or design project.
She wrote a quick rough draft of her essay before editing grammar, spelling and sentence structure.
safe haven
A place of safety, refuge or security from danger, harm, persecution or difficulty.
The peaceful nature reserve provided a safe haven for endangered bird species fleeing habitat destruction.
social distance
The physical space maintained between individuals to prevent infection or maintain personal boundaries.
Maintaining adequate social distance in crowded public places helps reduce the risk of spreading airborne illnesses.
sustainable development
Economic development conducted carefully without depletion of natural resources for future human generations.
The urban plan prioritized sustainable development by building energy-efficient houses and expanding green park areas.
unintended consequence
An outcome or result that was not foreseen or intended by an initial action or decision.
Traffic congestion on local residential streets was an unintended consequence of closing the main city bridge.
urban sprawl
The uncontrolled expansion of urban areas into surrounding rural or countryside territory.
Rapid urban sprawl swallowed up agricultural land and put pressure on countryside wildlife habitats around the city.
valuable insight
Deep, helpful and accurate understanding gained about a complex topic or human behavior.
The customer survey provided valuable insight into how young people preferred to shop for clothes online.
vast majority
An overwhelming or very large percentage of a total group of people or things.
The vast majority of local residents supported plans to create a new pedestrian area in town.
work-life balance
The equilibrium between time and effort devoted to work and personal personal lifestyle activities.
Achieving a healthy work-life balance helps employees reduce stress and spend quality time with their families.
backseat driver
A passenger in a vehicle who offers unwanted advice or criticism to the driver.
Her father was a terrible backseat driver, constantly warning her about road signs and speed limits.
busy bee
An energetic, active person who is always busily occupied with various tasks.
She was a real busy bee, spending her Saturday morning baking cakes and tidying the whole house.
couch potato
A person who takes little exercise and spends much time watching television sitting down.
Instead of remaining a couch potato on weekends, he decided to join a local running club.
dark horse
A person who keeps their talents or interests secret but surprises others with success.
He proved to be a dark horse by winning the chess tournament despite never entering competitions before.
eager beaver
An enthusiastic person who is extremely hard-working and keen to perform tasks.
The new intern was an eager beaver, arriving early every morning and offering to help everyone.
early bird
A person who habitually gets up or arrives early in the morning.
Being an early bird, she enjoyed going for a peaceful walk before the city woke up.
fair-weather friend
A person who is only a friend when circumstances are pleasant and easy.
He realized she was a fair-weather friend when she disappeared as soon as he needed support.
food for thought
Something that provides serious material for reflection, deep intellectual analysis or careful mental consideration.
The documentary about marine conservation provided plenty of food for thought for students studying environmental science.
fresh start
An opportunity to begin again in a new way, free from past mistakes or problems.
Moving to a new coastal town offered her a fresh start after leaving her old corporate job.
golden handshake
A large payment given to a senior executive upon leaving a company or retiring.
The retiring chief officer received a substantial golden handshake when he stepped down from his position.
night owl
A person who prefers to stay up late at night and works best during evening hours.
As a night owl, he found it easiest to write his university essays past midnight.
off the cuff
Spoken, performed or done spontaneously without prior preparation, formal planning or written notes.
He delivered an entertaining speech off the cuff after being asked to speak at short notice.
rainy day
A possible future period of unexpected financial need, emergency, personal hardship or difficulty.
It is wise to save a portion of your monthly income for a rainy day in future.
sweet tooth
A strong liking or craving for sweet foods, such as chocolates and desserts.
Her strong sweet tooth meant she could never resist ordering chocolate cake after a restaurant meal.
time is money
A proverb emphasizing that time is a valuable resource and should not be wasted.
In fast-paced business environments, managers often remind employees that time is money during project execution.
apprentice
A person who is learning a trade from a skilled employer for an agreed period.
The young apprentice learned bricklaying skills while working alongside an experienced builder on site.
biodegradable
Capable of being decomposed by bacteria or other living organisms without polluting the environment.
The supermarket switched to using biodegradable packaging made from plant materials to reduce plastic waste.
bureaucracy
Excessively complicated administrative procedures, official rules and paper requirements in large organizations.
Excessive government bureaucracy delayed the approval of small business loans for several months.
cartel
An association of manufacturers or suppliers with the purpose of maintaining high market prices.
The international oil cartel agreed to reduce crude oil production to keep global fuel prices stable.
chancellor
A senior state or university official, especially the head of government in some countries.
The Chancellor of the Exchequer announced new economic measures during his speech to parliament today.
collaborate
To work jointly with others on an activity or project to achieve a shared goal.
Scientists from three European universities agreed to collaborate on a groundbreaking solar power research project.
commercialism
An emphasis on maximizing profit, commercial success or buying and selling goods in society.
Critics complained that the excessive commercialism of festive holidays damaged the traditional spirit of community celebrations.
concession
A thing that is granted or yielded in response to demands during negotiations.
The management offered a salary concession to prevent factory workers from taking formal strike action.
conglomerate
A large corporation formed by merging diverse companies operating in entirely different industries.
The international media conglomerate owned newspaper publications, television channels and digital streaming platforms.
creditor
A person, bank or company to whom money is owed by a debtor.
The failing business owed several thousand pounds to its primary creditor after missing loan repayments.
debtor
A person, organization or country that owes a sum of money to a creditor.
The court ordered the debtor to establish a monthly repayment plan to clear outstanding financial obligations.
delegation
A body of delegates representing a country or organization at an official conference.
The diplomatic delegation arrived in Geneva to attend international trade talks with foreign government leaders.
demographics
Statistical data relating to the population and particular groups within it, such as age.
Changing city demographics showed a significant increase in young working professionals moving to urban centers.
disinvestment
The reduction of non-current assets or selling off capital investments by a company.
The board decided on disinvestment from fossil fuel projects to reallocate capital into renewable energy technologies.
downsizing
The reduction of the size of a company or workforce to cut operating costs.
Corporate downsizing resulted in the closure of two regional offices and lost jobs for fifty employees.
embargo
An official ban on trade or other commercial activity with a particular foreign country.
The international community imposed a strict trade embargo on weapons sales to the warring country.
endorser
A person who publicly approves or supports a product, brand, candidate or policy.
The famous athlete signed a lucrative contract to become the main brand endorser for sportswear.
equity
The value of shares issued by a company or ownership value in property.
She built up substantial equity in her home after making regular mortgage payments for fifteen years.
ethnicity
Statistical data or personal background relating to racial, national or cultural social groups.
The survey asked respondents to state their country of birth, language and ethnicity.
expatriate
A person who lives outside their native country, often for professional employment reasons.
Many expatriate workers living in Dubai enjoy the warm climate and vibrant international community environment.
expenditure
An amount of money spent by a government, organization or individual during a period.
The council promised to cut unnecessary public expenditure to avoid increasing local property taxes.
feasibility
The state or degree of being easily or conveniently done or practically achieved.
Engineers conducted a detailed feasibility study before recommending the construction of a new bridge.
fluctuation
An irregular rising and falling in number, amount or level of something over time.
Unpredictable currency fluctuation made it difficult for import businesses to forecast their quarterly operating profits.
foreclosure
The action of taking possession of a mortgaged property when payments are missed.
The bank initiated foreclosure proceedings after the homeowner failed to pay mortgage installments for six months.
forensics
Scientific tests or techniques used in connection with the detection of crime evidence.
Police forensics experts examined digital computer files to gather evidence for the financial fraud investigation.
grievance
A real or imagined cause for complaint, especially unfair treatment at work.
The trade union filed a formal employee grievance regarding unsafe working conditions inside the warehouse.
guarantor
A person or organization that gives a guarantee to pay a debt if required.
Her parents agreed to act as a financial guarantor so she could rent her first London apartment.
headquarters
The main administrative center or central office of an organization or business corporation.
The multinational technology firm moved its European headquarters to a modern office complex in Dublin.
hierarchy
A system in which members of an organization are ranked according to status.
The corporate organizational hierarchy placed senior executive directors above department managers and administrative operational staff.
incentivise
To motivate or encourage someone to do something by offering rewards or benefits.
The government introduced tax credits to incentivise small businesses to invest in green energy technologies.
indemnity
Security or protection against a loss or other financial liability under an insurance contract.
The insurance policy provided full indemnity against accidental property damage caused by flooding or fire.
infrastructure
The basic physical and organizational structures needed for the operation of a society.
Investing in public transport infrastructure reduced urban traffic congestion and improved travel times across the region.
insolvency
The state of being unable to pay debts owed, leading to legal financial proceedings.
Poor sales and mounting unpaid bills forced the small manufacturing business into immediate formal insolvency.
intermediary
A person who acts as a link between people in order to bring about agreement.
An independent intermediary helped negotiate a settlement between the union representatives and management board members.
inventory
A complete list of items such as property, goods in stock or contents of a building.
The warehouse manager conducted a monthly inventory check to ensure stock levels matched digital sales records.
jurisdiction
The official power to make legal decisions and judgments over an area or domain.
The local court did not hold legal jurisdiction over offenses committed outside national territorial borders.
liability
The state of being legally responsible for something, or an outstanding financial debt obligation.
The company accepted full financial liability for the accidental chemical spill and agreed to clean the river.
liquidation
The process of closing a business and converting its assets into cash to pay debts.
When the retail chain collapsed, its remaining store stock was sold off during a final liquidation sale.
litigation
The process of taking legal action through a court of law to settle disputes.
Protracted corporate litigation between the two software companies lasted three years before a settlement was reached.
lucrative
Producing a great deal of profit or financial gain for an individual or business.
Selling hand-crafted furniture online proved to be a highly lucrative business venture for the creative artisan.
macroeconomics
The branch of economics concerned with large-scale or general economic factors of a nation.
Students taking macroeconomics analyzed how interest rates and inflation affect national employment and consumer spending.
malpractice
Improper, illegal or negligent professional activity or treatment by a doctor or lawyer.
The surgeon faced serious allegations of medical malpractice following a series of botched surgical operations.
microeconomics
The part of economics concerned with single factors and the effects of individual decisions.
In microeconomics, students study how supply and demand influence prices for individual consumer goods.
milestone
An action or event marking a significant stage or development in a project.
Reaching one million active users was a major milestone for the young social media startup.
misconduct
Unacceptable or improper behavior, especially by a professional or person in authority.
The police officer was suspended following allegations of serious professional misconduct during the investigation.
mitigation
The action of reducing the severity, seriousness or painfulness of something undesirable.
Installing emergency flood barriers was a key mitigation strategy to protect coastal homes from rising sea levels.
mortgagee
The lender in a mortgage agreement, typically a bank or financial building society.
The mortgagee held legal rights to the property until the home loan was paid off completely.
mortgagor
A borrower who puts up property as security for a loan under a mortgage.
The mortgagor made regular monthly payments to the building society to clear her home loan debt.
nepotism
The practice among those with power of favoring relatives or friends, especially by giving jobs.
Employees complained of nepotism when the director appointed his unqualified son to senior manager.
net worth
The total value of all assets owned by an individual or business minus all liabilities.
Her estimated net worth increased after she invested in commercial real estate properties in the city.
outsourcing
Obtaining goods or services from an outside or foreign supplier, especially in place of internal resources.
Outsourcing customer service call centers to foreign countries helped the telecom company cut operational overheads.
overdraft
A deficit in a bank account caused by drawing more money than the account holds.
She used an agreed bank overdraft to cover unexpected car repair expenses until her next payday.
patent
A government authority conferring a right or title for a set period to exclude others from making an invention.
The inventor secured a patent for his innovative solar water purification system to protect his design.
philanthropy
The desire to promote the welfare of others, expressed especially by the generous donation of money.
Through personal philanthropy, the wealthy industrialist funded the construction of three public university libraries.
precedent
An earlier event or action that is regarded as an example or guide in similar circumstances.
The court ruling set a historic precedent for future legal cases involving digital copyright infringement.
privatisation
The transfer of a business, industry or service from public to private ownership and control.
The privatisation of national railway services led to debates about ticket prices and service reliability.
propaganda
Information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view.
State television broadcast political propaganda to influence public opinion during the national parliamentary election campaign.
protectionism
The theory or practice of shielding a country's domestic industries from foreign competition by taxing imports.
Government protectionism policies involved placing high import tariffs on foreign steel to support local factories.
protocol
The official system of rules and acceptable behavior that governs procedures in official situations.
Diplomats followed strict official protocol when welcoming the visiting head of state at the airport.
ransomware
A type of malicious software designed to block access to a computer system until money is paid.
A severe ransomware attack locked hospital computer systems, forcing staff to use paper patient records.
ratification
The official way to confirm something, usually by vote, making an agreement formally valid.
Parliamentary ratification of the international peace treaty was required before diplomatic relations could resume officially.
rationing
The controlled distribution of scarce resources, goods or food supplies during an emergency or war.
Fuel rationing was introduced across the country during the severe winter oil supply shortage.
recession
A period of temporary economic decline during which trade and industrial activity are reduced.
During the economic recession, consumer spending dropped significantly and many small retail businesses closed.
reconciliation
The restoration of friendly relations or the action of making financial accounts consistent.
The council promoted peace and reconciliation between the two conflicting ethnic communities after years of tension.
regulator
A person or body that supervises a particular industry or business activity to enforce rules.
The independent financial regulator fined the bank for failing to protect customer data from fraud.
reimbursement
Repayment of money spent by an employee or individual on business expenses or official duties.
She submitted her travel receipts to the finance department to receive full financial reimbursement for her trip.
remittance
A sum of money sent, especially by mail or digital transfer, in payment for goods or services.
Overseas workers sent monthly monetary remittance payments back home to support their families living in rural villages.
renovation
The action of renovating a building or structure to restore it to good condition.
The old Victorian theatre underwent extensive interior renovation to modernize seating and stage lighting systems.
restructuring
Reorganizing the operational or financial structure of a company to make it more efficient.
Corporate restructuring led to the merging of two administrative departments and reduced monthly business overheads.
retailer
A person or business that sells goods to the public in relatively small quantities for immediate consumption.
Major clothing retailer stores launched end-of-season sales discounts to clear remaining stock before autumn.
retrenchment
The reduction of costs or spending in response to economic difficulty or business losses.
The university announced a period of financial retrenchment, cutting research grants and freezing staff recruitment.
revocation
The official cancellation or withdrawal of a decree, decision, licence or legal personal privilege.
The driver faced immediate revocation of his driving licence following repeated dangerous speeding offenses.
scarcity
The state of being scarce or in short supply, a shortage of essential resources.
Water scarcity during the prolonged summer drought forced local authorities to restrict lawn watering.
scrutiny
Critical observation, close inspection or careful examination of details, actions, records or public statements.
The politician's business dealings came under intense public scrutiny following allegations of financial corruption.
shareholding
A quantity of shares held by a shareholder in a business corporation.
She sold her majority shareholding in the publishing firm after deciding to retire from business.
slump
A sudden severe or prolonged fall in the price, value or amount of something.
A sudden slump in global oil prices harmed economic growth in oil-exporting nations.
solvency
The possession of assets exceeding liabilities, the ability to pay one's debts.
The auditor confirmed the financial solvency of the insurance company after reviewing its annual accounting books.
speculation
Forming a theory without firm evidence, or financial investment in hope of gain but risk of loss.
Wild financial speculation in the property market created an unsustainable housing price bubble in the city.
spokesperson
A person nominated to speak on behalf of another person, group or organization.
A government spokesperson delivered an official statement regarding the new public health guidelines on television.
stagnation
Lack of activity, growth, development or progress in an economy or business.
Economic stagnation over three years caused rising unemployment and reduced consumer confidence across the country.
tariff
A tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports.
The government introduced a high protective tariff on imported agricultural goods to support local farmers.
tender
A formal offer to execute work or supply goods at a fixed stated price.
Construction firms submitted competitive written tender proposals to build the new city library complex.
testament
Something that serves as a sign or evidence of a specified fact, event or quality.
The school's excellent exam results are a clear testament to the hard work of teachers and students.
